title: BN10 inherited four-key amplified-boomerang estimate on full AES-192

display.name: Four-key amplified boomerang / inherited rough estimate

target.description: All12 AES-192 rounds under BN10 Figure3 and inherited BK09 Section6/Figure8 interval, including the standard final-round linear-layer convention. This is separate from the disputed11-round simple characteristic.

setting.key_relation: Four related secret keys in the inherited BK09 Section6.1 quartet construction; BN10 changes the top characteristic and retains the bottom. Relations are source-defined at round-key levels, not four arbitrary fixed-XOR master-key relations.
setting.plaintext_model: The inherited amplified-boomerang procedure uses chosen plaintext encryptions under four related keys (BK09 Section6.2). BN10 gives a new total data estimate2^116 without a new per-key/structure allocation.
assumptions: BN10 Section3.3 gives a rough2^7 improvement by changing the top trail and retaining the bottom framework; its charged pq exponent is48 versus55.
BK09 Section6.2 uses encryption-only amplified boomerang data. CPA+adaptiveCCA was an incorrect baseline inheritance for this AES-192 endpoint.
No full new phase-by-phase proof, memory budget, or numerical complete-key success is supplied by BN10.

time.note: Author-reported rough estimate2^169, a2^7 improvement over BK09. The local quartet-count formula supports the probability/data scaling, not a separately reproduced implementation.

data.note: Author-reported rough total2^116 chosen-plaintext encryptions under the inherited four-key amplified framework. No per-key distribution is newly specified.

memory.note: BN10 does not recalculate memory for the improved parameters. BK09 Table1 memory2^152 belongs to the earlier attack and is not copied into this point.

preprocessing.note: The source does not separately quantify this resource for this configuration.

success.description: Section3.3 only gives a rough2^7 improvement over the inherited BK09 amplified attack, not a numerical complete-key success. Its printed2^-48 quantity is the charged product of the upper/lower characteristics (pq convention, versus2^-55 before), not an independently justified full rectangle success. The data/time budget and inherited key relations remain unchanged.

review.scope: Targeted exact-edition success audit of defining construction and parameter passages, not a new full-paper or forward-literature audit. Source local/conditional models, expected counts, key-relation construction and full recovery remain separate.

components.description: PDF13: the changed top characteristic charges three active S-boxes at2^-6. Derived from the explicit3=2+1 count; no independent joint proof.
PDF13: the bottom characteristic charges five active S-boxes at2^-6. Derived from the explicit1+1+2+1 count.
PDF13: printed2^-(6*(2+1+1+1+2+1)), compared with2^-55 in BK09. This charged pq product is NOT the full amplified rectangle probability or aggregate key-recovery success.

evidence.interpretation: Primary table and defining text checked. Unknown costs are retained rather than preventing extraction.

evidence.interpretation: Section6.2 expressly encrypts under KA,KC and complements under KB,KD; no ciphertext-decryption queries. The four-key count and chosen-plaintext access follow this primary procedure.

evidence.locator: PDF p.13 / printed p.334, Section3.3; PDF p.21 / printed p.342 Figure3.
evidence.interpretation: The new top contributes18 and bottom30 to pq exponent48; inherited expected-quartet arithmetic preserves2^4 quartets when the data exponent decreases by7. This is bounded arithmetic, not a new full attack proof.

Its printed2^-48 quantity is the charged product of the upper/lower characteristics (pq convention, versus2^-55 before), not an independently justified full rectangle success. limitations: The11-round31-active simple characteristic is separately reported inconsistent in GMS17; no evidence identifies this correction with BN10 Figure3 full12-round boomerang.
Time/data remain the authors rough inherited estimates; memory/setup and complete-key success remain unknown.
Local expected-quartet formulas include the squared amplified probabilities and do not independently certify all key-ranking phases.
